Subject: Post-call: model fit + quantization tradeoffs (next steps)

Hi Jordan — great speaking with you this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on our discovery: 

Recap:
- Goal: deploy a conversational assistant for field ops that can summarize maintenance logs and answer safety/procedure questions. Target latency < 350ms p95 for short queries, and throughput to handle spikes at shift change.
- Data sensitivity: internal operational logs, PII redaction required, SOC2 scope requested.
- Evaluation priorities: safety/accuracy on procedural prompts, hallucination rate on short answers, and end-to-end latency.

Model & quantization recommendations (high level):
- Tier 1 (quality-first): Llama-3 70B fp16 (recommended for initial evals, best out-of-the-box accuracy)
- Tier 2 (balanced): Llama-3 70B + AWQ 4-bit (good throughput improvements with limited quality drop for our prompt set)
- Tier 3 (cost/throughput): Llama-3 70B + GPTQ/FP8 profiles (highest throughput, greater QA needed on safety prompts)

Attachments / links I shared:
- acme_eval_prompt_set.csv (sample prompt sets we used in the call)
- redwood_benchmark_results_20261115.pdf (internal perf/quality run vs common models)
- quant_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx (summary of AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 tradeoffs)
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-acme-evals

Proposed next steps:
1) You: confirm which evaluation metric you want prioritized (accuracy on safety prompts vs latency).
2) We: run two small evals (1k prompts) across the three configs above and share a concise tradeoff table + sample failure cases. ETA: 3 business days once you approve scope.
3) If results look good, schedule a short technical sync with your infra team to discuss deployment modes (Dedicated vs Private VPC) and initial capacity targets.

Questions for you now:
- Which is more important for Phase 1: strict latency SLO or minimizing false positives on safety-related prompts?
- Any constraints on on-prem hardware or key management we should know about?

Thanks — I’ll queue the evals as soon as you confirm the primary metric.

Best,

Great — I’ll take point. Quick notes on tradeoffs to set expectations: 

- AWQ (4-bit)
  - Pros: ~2.5-3x throughput increase vs fp16 in our infra; small quality delta on general prompts (~1-3% A/B drop), often negligible on structured prompts if calibrated.
  - Cons: can surface subtle tokenization/regression issues on edge-case safety prompts; requires per-model per-workload calibration.

- GPTQ (8-bit)
  - Pros: conservative quantization, lower risk of regression; reasonable throughput gains (~1.4-1.8x).
  - Cons: less aggressive cost savings than AWQ.

- FP8 experimental
  - Pros: potential for high throughput and lower memory footprint; still early and hardware-dependent.
  - Cons: riskier for safety-sensitive prompts; profiling required to ensure numerical stability.

Proposed evaluation plan we’ll run:
- 1k safety-focused prompts from acme_eval_prompt_set.csv
- 3 model configs: fp16 baseline, AWQ4, GPTQ8; FP8 if stable on our test infra
- Metrics: exact-match safety failures, hallucination rate (annotated), avg token latency, p95 latency, top failure examples (annotated)
- Deliverables: quant_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx + redwood_benchmark_results_20261115.pdf (sample format).

I attached the initial tradeoff workbook template and will push raw logs to the Drive link once runs complete.
